Open Start and type your company name and your own limits in the yellow cells: the days a patch test and a consent form stay valid, the days before a client counts as lapsed, the deposit and the tier levels.

Check Clients. Each row is a client with the allergy note they gave, the patch test and the consent form with their dates. The tier, the days since the last visit and the readiness for the next visit fill in.
Keep Appointments up to date from your booking system export. An upcoming visit shows a flag when the client's patch test or consent form is still due.
Write every patch test, consent form and allergy review on Safety Records. A patch test is a small test of a product on a small area of skin before a service, kept as a dated checklist.
Use Patch Test Schedule and First Visits before a new client comes: they show what is missing and how many days are left to fix it.
Watch Consent Renewals and Allergy Notes. The days left and the review flag tell you which forms and notes need attention. Check your own local rules on how long a form stays valid.
Log before and after photos as text on Photo Log with the client's agreement to share. Keep preferences, notes and tags on their own sheets.
Record every redo request on Redo and Fix Log and every request about a client's data on Data Requests. Use Duplicate Check to merge records that belong to one client.
Read Client Months, Client Segments and Client Sources to see new and returning clients, the tiers and where clients come from.
Use the 14 calculators for client value, rebooking dates, patch test and consent validity, first-visit readiness, the cost of a new client, birthday offers and referrals.
Read the Clients and Records Dashboard and the Charts every week: patch tests, consent forms, redo requests, data requests and the new clients of the month.

Clients with days since the last visit and rebooking state
One row per client: visits, spend, usual technician and service, next appointment and next due date; days since the last visit, the lapsed flags and the rebooking state fill in by themselves.
One row per appointment: date, technician, service, client, status, price, promotion used and whether the client booked the next visit; the completed and rebooked flags fill in by themselves.
Fills due with nudge state and days overdue
One row per client visit that needs a fill, infill or series visit: last visit, cycle days, due date and the nudge sent; days overdue, the fill state and the revenue at risk fill in by themselves.
Rebooking desk log with days to the next visit
One row per visit that ended at the front desk: whether the client booked the next visit there, the reason and the next date; days to the next visit and the desk result fill in by themselves.
One row per technician and month: appointments, rebooked visits, new clients, no-shows and revenue; the rebooking rate, the visits short of the target and the rate check fill in by themselves.
One row per message sent to a client: date, kind, channel, status and who sent it; the replied flag fills in by itself. Use it to see which nudges, offers and requests get answers.
Message templates with sends and reply rate
The twelve standard messages with the trigger, channel and days after the trigger (negative means before); messages sent in the last 30 days and the reply rate of each kind fill in by themselves.
Win-back offers with outcome and revenue

One row per win-back offer (an offer to a client who stopped coming): client, days lapsed, service, offer percent, channel, result and revenue; the returned flag, days to book and the outcome fill in.
One row per client who has not been seen for 60 days or more and has nothing booked: visits, spend, usual service and technician and the win-back offer sent; days lapsed and the offer state fill in.
Referral reward ledger with days pending
One row per referral: the client who sent a friend, the new client, the first service, the reward and its status; days pending, the amount owed and the reward check fill in by themselves.
Referral rules with the gap to the standard reward
The six referral rules with the reward and who they apply to; keep them in step with the standard reward in Start.
Reviews with reply deadline and rating check
One row per review: client, technician, service, rating, source, topic, reply status and the reply date; days to reply (or waiting), the reply check and the rating check fill in by themselves.
Review requests with the response flag
One row per review request sent after a visit: client, appointment, channel, result and the rating given; the responded flag and the result check fill in by themselves.
Review sources with count and average
The five places a review can come from; the number of reviews and the average rating of each fill in by themselves.
One row per promotion: kind, dates, discount percent, visits redeemed, revenue and discount given; net gain, the status and the discount per visit fill in by themselves.
The usual days between visits for each of the 20 services and the grace days; the category, the weeks and the fills still open for the service fill in by themselves.
Team and outside contacts with rebooking and review results
The owner, technicians, front desk and outside contacts with phone and e-mail; rebooking rate and review average of the last three months, open fills and lapsed clients fill in by themselves.
Services with cycle days and review average
The 20 services with category, minutes and price; the cycle days, the fills open, the reviews and the review average of each service fill in by themselves.
Low rating follow-ups with days open
One row per low rating that needs a fix: client, technician, rating, issue, action and status; days open, the open flag and the follow-up check fill in by themselves.
Nudge schedule for a fill that is due
The eight steps after a fill due date: days after the due date and the channel; follow them in order until the client rebooks or moves to win-back.
